Thanks for the review @hoxyq!

I've updated the PR to address the gap in the backend DevTools `Store` logic rather than just swallowing the error.

### Root Cause
Specifically, when a `Suspense` component is filtered out by the user's component filter preferences, the backend DevTools agent correctly drops its mount operation (yielding no `SUSPENSE_TREE_OPERATION_ADD` operation). However, when the children of this filtered suspense boundary are later reordered, the backend agent was still pushing a `SUSPENSE_TREE_OPERATION_REORDER_CHILDREN` operation containing the ID of the filtered node (coerced/cast as `0` since it has a `FilteredFiberInstance` kind). This caused the frontend `Store` to attempt to resolve node `0` from `_idToSuspense`, resulting in the `Cannot reorder children for suspense node "0" because no matching node was found in the Store` crash.

### Solution
1. Added an early return to `recordResetSuspenseChildren` in `packages/react-devtools-shared/src/backend/fiber/renderer.js` if the parent instance is filtered (i.e. `kind !== FIBER_INSTANCE`), matching the early return behavior in `recordSuspenseResize` and `recordSuspenseSuspenders`.
2. Added a test suite `should not throw when reordering children of filtered Suspense boundary` in `packages/react-devtools-shared/src/__tests__/storeComponentFilters-test.js` to verify that reordering children of a filtered Suspense boundary runs cleanly and does not trigger any error/crash.
